# WorldScape3DRegion

**Inherits:** [Resource](Resource.md) **\<** [RefCounted](RefCounted.md) **\<** [Object](Object.md)

<!-- classref-introduction-group -->

## Description

This resource stores all map data for WorldScape3D.

## Property Descriptions

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_color_map"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Image](Image.md) **color_map** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_color_map)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_color_map**\ (\ value\: [Image](Image.md)\ )
- [Image](Image.md) **get_color_map**\ (\ )

This map is used to paint color that blends in to the terrain textures.

Image format: FORMAT_RGBA8, 32-bits per pixel as four 8-bit components.

\ **RGB** is used for color, which is multiplied by albedo in the shader. Multiply is a blend mode that only darkens.

\ **A** is used for a roughness modifier. A value of 0.5 means no change to the existing texture roughness. Higher than this value increases roughness, lower decreases it.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_control_map"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Image](Image.md) **control_map** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_control_map)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_control_map**\ (\ value\: [Image](Image.md)\ )
- [Image](Image.md) **get_control_map**\ (\ )

This map tells the shader which textures to use where, how to blend, where to place holes, etc.

Image format: FORMAT_RF, 32-bit per pixel as full-precision floating-point.

However, we interpret these images as format: [RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_R32_UINT](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-constant-data-format-r32-uint) aka OpenGL RG32UI 32-bit per pixel as unsigned integer. See [Control map format](https://terrain3d.readthedocs.io/en/stable/docs/controlmap_format.html).

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_deleted"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[bool](bool.md) **deleted** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_deleted)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_deleted**\ (\ value\: [bool](bool.md)\ )
- [bool](bool.md) **is_deleted**\ (\ )

This region is marked for deletion. It won't be rendered once [WorldScape3DData.update_maps()](WorldScape3DData.md#WorldScape3DData_method_update_maps) rebuilds the map index. The file will be deleted from disk on [save()](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_method_save).

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_edited"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[bool](bool.md) **edited** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_edited)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_edited**\ (\ value\: [bool](bool.md)\ )
- [bool](bool.md) **is_edited**\ (\ )

This region is marked for updating by [WorldScape3DData.update_maps()](WorldScape3DData.md#WorldScape3DData_method_update_maps) and for undo/redo tracking while the terrain is being edited. This flag serves a different purpose than [modified](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_property_modified).

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_height_map"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Image](Image.md) **height_map** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_height_map)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_height_map**\ (\ value\: [Image](Image.md)\ )
- [Image](Image.md) **get_height_map**\ (\ )

This map contains the real value heights for the terrain.

Image format: FORMAT_RF, 32-bit per pixel as full-precision floating-point.

Heights sent to the vertex shader on the GPU which modifies the mesh in real-time.

Editing is always done in 32-bit. We do provide an option to save as 16-bit, see [WorldScape3D.save_16_bit](WorldScape3D.md#WorldScape3D_property_save_16_bit).

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_height_range"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Vector2](Vector2.md) **height_range** = `Vector2(0, 0)` [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_height_range)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_height_range**\ (\ value\: [Vector2](Vector2.md)\ )
- [Vector2](Vector2.md) **get_height_range**\ (\ )

The current minimum and maximum height range for this region, used to calculate the AABB of the terrain. Update it with [update_height()](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_method_update_height), and recalculate it with [calc_height_range()](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_method_calc_height_range).

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_instances"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Dictionary](Dictionary.md) **instances** = `{}` [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_instances)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_instances**\ (\ value\: [Dictionary](Dictionary.md)\ )
- [Dictionary](Dictionary.md) **get_instances**\ (\ )

A Dictionary that stores the instancer transforms for this region.

The format is instances{mesh_id:int} -&gt; cells{grid_location:Vector2i} -&gt; ( Array:Transform3D, PackedColorArray, modified:bool ). That is:

- A Dictionary keyed by mesh_id that returns:

- A Dictionary keyed by the grid location of the 32 x 32m cell that returns:

- A 3-item Array that contains:

- 0: An Array of Transform3Ds

- 1: A PackedColorArray with instance colors, same index as above

- 2: A bool that tracks if this cell has been modified

After changing this data, call [WorldScape3DInstancer.update_mmis()](WorldScape3DInstancer.md#WorldScape3DInstancer_method_update_mmis) to rebuild the MMIs.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_location"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[Vector2i](Vector2i.md) **location** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_location)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_location**\ (\ value\: [Vector2i](Vector2i.md)\ )
- [Vector2i](Vector2i.md) **get_location**\ (\ )

The location in region grid space ``(world space / region_size)`` coordinates. e.g. (-1, 1) equates to (-1024, 1024) in world space given a [region_size](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_property_region_size) of 1024.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_modified"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[bool](bool.md) **modified** [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_modified)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_modified**\ (\ value\: [bool](bool.md)\ )
- [bool](bool.md) **is_modified**\ (\ )

This region has been modified and will be saved to disk upon [save()](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_method_save). This serves a different purpose than the temporary [edited](WorldScape3DRegion.md#WorldScape3DRegion_property_edited) setting.

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_region_size"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[int](int.md) **region_size** = `0` [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_region_size)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_region_size**\ (\ value\: [int](int.md)\ )

The current region size for this region, calculated from the dimensions of the first loaded map. It should match [WorldScape3D.region_size](WorldScape3D.md#WorldScape3D_property_region_size).

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_version"></a>

[float](float.md) **version** = `0.8` [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_version)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

<hr class="classref-item-separator"/>

<a id="WorldScape3DRegion_property_vertex_spacing"></a>

<!-- classref-property -->

[float](float.md) **vertex_spacing** = `1.0` [🔗](#WorldScape3DRegion_property_vertex_spacing)

<!-- classref-property-setget -->

- `void` **set_vertex_spacing**\ (\ value\: [float](float.md)\ )
- [float](float.md) **get_vertex_spacing**\ (\ )

Stored instancer transforms are laterally scaled by this value. This value is manage by the instancer on loading or when [WorldScape3D.vertex_spacing](WorldScape3D.md#WorldScape3D_property_vertex_spacing) is set, and shouldn't be manually adjusted.

Saves this region to the current file name.

- path - specifies a directory and file name to use from now on.

- 16-bit - save this region with 16-bit height map instead of 32-bit. This process is lossy. Does not change the bit depth in memory.
